deviations: split_region2_partial_overlap_refuses premise: the packet says b's disk r=1.5 circle 'crosses the hole circle r=1 twice', but the two circles are CONCENTRIC (both centered at (2,2)) and never intersect (BG-NUM-002 check). The Region2 screen classifies the pair as PARTIAL OVERLAP instead: a boundary sample of the r=1.5 disk lies strictly inside a's top-face region (the annulus ring r in [1, 1.5]) while the disk's interior wraps a's hole, so neither region contains the other. The call refuses UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred) as the packet requires.

FF open-arc endpoint certification is interpreted GEOMETRICALLY: a curve x boundary crossing is certified when a certified Point event's 3-D locus lies within tol of the crossing point, regardless of which face's boundary edges the event names. This is what lets the two shared generator lines enter b's cylinder wall in split_open_arc_uses_point_events_for_trimming (the four Point events name a's side-face edges, but their 3-D points also lie on b's rim circles).
Face::debug_new (the divide_face pattern) is banned in added kernel lines by GATE-3 (H-4: no debug-vs-release validity split), so divide_one_face builds fragments with Face::new_unchecked.

The booked import list (use crate::{Curve, Point3, Surface}; use truck_evidence::contact::{ContactDimension, ContactEventKind}) does not resolve: truck-shapeops does not re-export the geometry types at its root and truck-evidence's contact module imports ContactDimension/ContactEventKind privately from truck-base. The booked TYPES (SolidRef, StratumRef, ContactEvent, FragmentMesh, ...) are realized exactly with the booked field names; the imports resolve through truck_geometry::canonical, truck_base::cgmath64, and truck_base::contact.

Region2 containment uses a boundary-point AND an interior-representative test (the packet's single 'a boundary sample point of one face inside the other's region' test is insufficient when the contained face wraps a hole of the containing face, cf. the test-5 derivation in deviations[0]).

notes: Landed vendor/truck/truck-shapeops/src/boolean/split.rs (new module, `pub mod split;` in boolean/mod.rs after the doc header), plus the truck-evidence dependency line in Cargo.toml (and the refreshed Cargo.lock). The booked types (SolidRef, StratumRef, ContactEvent, FragmentOrigin, Fragment, AdjacencyParity, FragmentAdjacency, CoincidentOrientation, CoincidentPair, FragmentMesh, split_fragments) are verbatim; every ContactLocus/AnalyticIntersection/ExactCurve arm is matched exhaustively with no `_` arm. FLAGSHIP EXACT COUNTS (split_flagship_top_face_by_ff_circle): 10 fragments (a block: bottom 1, top 2 [annulus = square wire (4 edges) + hole wire (the same two rim half-edges inverted); disk = one wire of the two rim half-edges], 4 sides 1 each = 7; b disk: bottom cap 1, top cap 1, wall 1 = 3). adjacency = 17 entries: 2 Flip (disk <-> annulus, once per shared rim half-edge) + 15 Same (a: annulus<->4 sides 4, bottom<->4 sides 4, side<->side seams 4; b: wall<->top cap 2 [the two rim halves], wall<->bottom cap 1); no cross-solid pair in adjacency. coincident = 1: {a: a's disk fragment, b: b's top-cap fragment, Identical} (both faces orientation()==true). The two rim half-edge INSTANCES are EdgeID-identical across the disk, the annulus hole wire, b's wall top wire and b's top-cap wire (the sewing-oracle cut propagated by swap_edge_into_wire). Other tests: split_cuts_edges_at_point_contacts (top face stays 1 fragment, 5-edge wire, vertex at (2,0,2), top<->front-side Same once per half); split_open_arc_uses_point_events_for_trimming (x=4 side -> 3 strips, bottom/top edges 3 segments each, two shared line arcs, 2 Flip among a's side fragments and 4 total across both shells); split_region2_disjoint_regions_is_no_coincidence (no pair, no split); split_region2_partial_overlap_refuses and split_refuses_deferred_loci (both refuse ContactReductionDeferred). TOLERANCE-CLASS DECISIONS THAT SURPRISED ME: (1) Line::parameter_division returns only the two endpoints, so an open boundary-to-boundary arc would classify OnBoundary (all samples on the boundary); classify_curve enforces a minimum 24-sample uniform subdivision. (2) Periodic (cylinder) domains: a generator at u = -pi/2 measures pi/2 away from the rim polygon (u in [0, TAU]) unless the u coordinate is folded onto the principal branch (rem_euclid) before the on-boundary/containment tests. (3) Edge cuts must be applied to the ABSOLUTE clone (the loops_store pattern): cutting the oriented use hands swap_edge_into_wire a wire whose ends do not match the use's ends for inverted edges, and Wire::swap_edge_into_wire silently no-ops (returns false). (4) divide_one_face must be orientation-aware: on an inverted face (the extrude cylinder wall) the region wires have negative polygon area; the region test reads area < 0 for inverted faces and treats unattachable negative wires as regions in their own right. OLD SERVICES AS PATTERNS (RW3 verdict): yes - the loops_store/divide_face wire-mutation services are adequate as patterns, with the three corrections above (absolute-clone cut, orientation-aware divide, minimum-sampling classification). The emap/change_vertex vertex-unification machinery was NOT needed for the certified-witness path: cutting directly with per-certified-point canonical vertices suffices (each canonical vertex is created once per certified point and shared across both shells' cuts and the arc endpoints).
